name: Redwood Research (charityevals)
beneficiaries_note: Our build: an AI catastrophe kills people everywhere and the future lost is everyone's, so the result is spread by world population.
summary: Redwood Research (Berkeley) researches AI that works against its developers: it started AI control (keeping a model safe to use even if it tries to subvert its monitors), showed with Anthropic that a production model can fake alignment, and advises AI companies and the UK AI Security Institute. This model covers its one programme in 2024 ($2.9M spent), its own research and $0.68M that completed the spin-off of the Constellation research centre. At the defaults it averts about {{result}} years of healthy life per $1,000, from {{low}} to {{high}} in 90% of the simulation's draws, so the result is mostly uncertainty: each dollar is valued as a typical project's cut in the forecast risk of an AI catastrophe (Rethink Priorities' cross-cause model, the Existential Risk Persuasion Tournament's experts), deaths valued like every death and the future lost counted only where you count lives that never start (0% by default). All its work is against misaligned AI, and Rethink's typical misalignment project cuts the deaths in catastrophes the world survives far less per dollar than its typical misuse project; the next dollar counts at 40% of the past average because 2024 ran on over two years of reserves, though it buys only research now the spin-off is done. The chance of an AI catastrophe (the slider), the typical cut per dollar, the discount rate and the share of work counted as misuse (0 by default; counting the paper on hidden capabilities as misuse work would raise the result 15 times) are the biggest swings; the one branch is discounted for missing data: no outcome of the work on the risk is measured.

rows.label: AI: share of the AI spending on work against misuse (dangerous-capability evaluations, defences against misuse)
rows.explainer: The share of Redwood's AI spending that is work against misuse. None of its 2024 outputs is aimed at misuse: its research is on AI that works against its developers (AI control, alignment faking, hidden reasoning). Of the four outputs its research page dates to 2024 (password-locked models, alignment faking, adaptive deployment of untrusted models, and the control safety case, written with the UK AI Security Institute in 2024 and posted in January 2025), only the password-locked models paper could be read either way: it shows how to elicit capabilities a model hides, which serves dangerous-capability evaluations against misuse and evaluations of scheming models alike. Work aimed at both counts as misalignment (the template's rule), so 0 by that rule, stated as certain: the simulation does not draw it. Read as misuse work, that paper's share of the research spending would be about 15%: one of the four outputs (25% by count), but a smaller project than the control work or alignment faking (four authors, two of them Redwood's, Greenblatt and Roger, with Krasheninnikov and Krueger of Cambridge; arXiv 2405.19550), so about 15%.

rows.label: Research: how far the typical project's effect applies
rows.explainer: Redwood's research against Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project. Above typical: it started AI control as a field ('AI companies and other researchers have since built on this work', its home page says), it advises Google DeepMind and Anthropic on misaligned-AI risk, its alignment-faking study with Anthropic showed a production model (Claude 3 Opus) faking alignment in training, and it wrote a control safety case with the UK AI Security Institute, so its outputs go straight into how developers and a government institute test models. Below in how directly it acts: a protocol cuts the risk only once labs use it on their most capable models. 1.2, our judgment, 0.5 to 2.5, the family's upper bound for a typical dollar; the low end set by the direct uptake into labs' and a government's safety methods, the range wide because no lab says which protocols it runs.

rows.formula: (spend_research * research_evidence_adj + spend_grant_cash * grant_evidence_adj + spend_grant_leasehold * leasehold_evidence_adj) / program_spend
rows.explainer: How far Rethink Priorities' typical small AI project applies to Redwood's work: its research, the cash grant to Constellation and the transferred fit-out weighted by spending: about 0.96.

rows.label: Share of the work no one else would have done now
rows.explainer: The share of the work no one else would have done now: Redwood proposed AI control and is still its main independent group; labs' own teams (Anthropic's alignment stress-testing team co-wrote alignment faking) and the UK AI Security Institute now work on control too, partly because of it, and would have done some of this work anyway. Our judgment, 0.7 (0.4 to 0.9); that the work would have come later is in years_of_impact.

rows.label: Research: Redwood's share of the resources from people and groups it doesn't pay
rows.explainer: Outside resources behind the research evidence_adj is judged on: alignment faking had 20 authors, two of them Redwood's at publication (Greenblatt, Shlegeris; Roger was Redwood's until July 2024, 990 Part VII) and most of the rest Anthropic's, with Anthropic's models and compute; the control safety case was written with the UK AI Security Institute; outside scholars' time. Redwood's people led the work (Greenblatt is first author). 0.65, our judgment, 0.45 to 0.9: its largest 2024 result was a joint project with a lab.

rows.label: Constellation transfers: their share of the resources from people and groups they don't pay
rows.explainer: Outside resources behind the centre's outputs beyond what the grant pays, the speakers' and visitors' time: 0.85 (0.65 to 1), our judgment; that the visitors' research is paid by others is in grant_evidence_adj, not counted twice.

rows.label: This charity's share of the resources behind the outcome
rows.formula: (spend_research * research_evidence_adj * research_partner_share + spend_grant_cash * grant_evidence_adj * grant_partner_share + spend_grant_leasehold * leasehold_evidence_adj * grant_partner_share) / (program_spend * evidence_adj)
rows.explainer: Redwood's share of all resources behind its work: each part's partner share weighted by its spending times its evidence_adj, so the product with evidence_adj is each part's own (no fees: program service revenue $0, Part I line 9): about 0.67.

rows.label: This charity's share of the good done with money, work or budgets it brings in
rows.explainer: The site's one setting for resources another party commits only because of the organisation (docs/normalization.md 2.24): governments' budgets and enforcement, companies' compliance, the use others make of research. The charity is credited this share of the good done with them, net of their cost; the rest stays with those who paid or did the work. Fixed.

rows.label: Share of credit used
rows.explainer: The share among co-advocates times the mobiliser's share: the rest of the credit stays with those who carry out the result (docs/normalization.md 2.24).

rows.label: Leverage and funging
rows.explainer: Whether large funders (Open Philanthropy, now Coefficient Giving, almost its only funder) would give less if small donors gave more is the room factor of @next_dollar.redwood_research (docs/normalization.md 2.10), so it isn't asked again here (one question per adjustment): 1, our judgment, as for every catastrophic-risk model; 0.85 to 1.05 for funging the room factor misses.

rows.label: Counted less where the outcome isn't measured for this charity
rows.explainer: Thin: no outcome of Redwood's work on the risk is measured (papers, protocols and advice are outputs); the cut per dollar is a typical project's from Rethink Priorities' model and the chances are forecasts, so the shared missing-data step applies (docs/normalization.md 2.12).

rows.label: All adjustments combined
rows.explainer: The product of the adjustments above.

rows.label: Benefits not modelled, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Good beyond the catastrophes counted: control also guards against harms smaller than a catastrophe (an AI agent's sabotage or data theft inside a lab), and Redwood's researchers mentor outside scholars (MATS) and write much of the public strategy on control. 10% (0 to 30%) of the modelled value, our judgment.

rows.label: Harm: speeding up dangerous capabilities, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire (in the shared cut): control is meant to make it safe to use models that may be misaligned, so it can also let labs deploy more capable models sooner, or feel safe doing so. -5%, our judgment, down to -20%: the speed-up is control's stated use.

rows.label: Harm: information hazards and attention, as a share of modelled value
rows.explainer: Beyond a typical project's backfire: Redwood publishes the strategies a scheming model could use to beat monitors, and demonstrations of alignment faking, which future models may read in their training data. -2%, down to -10%, our judgment: these describe attacks on a lab's own monitoring rather than tools for misusers.
